Commentary.Commentary: The third innings is set to begin. England players stride out to the middle. Followed by KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma who will come out to bat for India. James Anderson to start with the ball. Rohit to face. Here we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

A good show with the ball for India! The visitors started on the right foot. The bowlers put the pressure straightaway on the hosts. It was Bumrah who started the proceedings, he picked up two wickets in a single over to get rid of the opening pair. Umesh Yadav was the pick of the bowlers as he picked up three wickets. All the bowlers found success during their spells. Jadeja snared two wickets. While Siraj and Thakur end with a single wicket each. The Indian batters will come out to bat for the remaining part of the session. India would hope, they remain unscathed before Stumps on Day 2. Do join us in a short while for the third innings.

England have fought hard! Unlike the last Test match, the opening pair of England could not do much about this time around, as both Burns and Hameed got skittled out in the same over. To add on to their misery, the hosts even lost Joe Root before Stumps on Day 1. Overton was the first one to depart on Day 2, and Malan followed him soon after. Then came two crucial stands of this innings which were between Pope and Bairstow followed by Pope and Ali. Which made sure England go past India’s total. Just after Tea, Pope was sent back on 81, he could not go onto make it a big one, but his team surely would be happy with his effort. The tail-enders added some crucial runs. Thanks to a brilliant knock by Chris Woakes of 50 runs, which helped his side to end their innings with a lead of 99 runs.

OUT! RUN OUT! And India finally get the last wicket. Short ball, around middle and leg. Woakes looks to scoop it over the keeper but he misses. Woakes is not even in a position to run but Anderson calls him through for the bye. Rishabh Pant collects the ball cleanly behind the sticks and he throws it back to Jasprit Bumrah who catches it and hits the stumps at the non-striker's end. Chris Woakes is well short of his crease and he is run out. England are all out with a lead of 99.
On a length, around off. Woakes plays late at it and guides it towards the slip cordon.

FOUR! Chris Woakes gets his FIFTY! What a Test match he is having. A full-length ball, on off. Woakes lifts it towards long on. The ball ends up in the boundary. A well deserved half-century for Chris Woakes.

Full and outside off. Woakes stays back and reaches out. The ball goes towards third man off the inside edge.
A length ball, on off. Woakes pushes it to cover.
Umesh bangs one short, around middle. James Anderson gets behind the line and blocks it.
Banged in short, around off. Woakes taps it to cover and collects a run this time.
Play and a miss! Good-length ball, outside off. Woakes swings hard but misses.

Leg bye! Banged in short, around off. James Anderson looks to defend but he misses and gets hit on the body. The battes sneak in a bye as the ball rolls away towards the off side.

FOUR! SMASHED! Good-length ball, outside off. Woakes makes room and smashes this one through covers for a boundary.

DRINKS! England seem to be running away with the lead and India are in a spot of bother as the lead is 85 now. But India have really done well, in the post-Tea session. They have picked up two wickets in the first hour of the final session. India will be desperate to hunt the final wicket down and make sure they get some time to bat before the stumps.

Not a good sight for Indian fans, as Jasprit Bumrah holds his calf and goes down on the ground. Maybe, it is just a cramp. The physio comes running out to have a look. This might take some time. Bumrah is fine to continue, says the physio.

OUT! BOWLED! Ravindra Jadeja strikes from the other end now! A tossed up delivery, around middle. Ollie Robinson gets low to slog sweep but he misses it completely as the ball turns away a bit and goes past his blade onto the stumps. Two wickets in quick succession here for India and they are right back in the game.

Huge wicket this for India in the context of this game as Pope was well set and marching along nicely. Thakur serves a good-length ball, outside off. Pope looks to guide it through third man but only manages an inside edge and the ball crashes onto the stumps. He is very disappointed with himself as he has to walk back after a hard-fought 81.

Who will bowl from the other end? It is going to be Ravindra Jadeja.

The final session is set to begin. The Indian players walk out to the middle. Followed by Ollie Pope and Chris Woakes who come out to bat for England. Jasprit Bumrah to start with the ball.

Not much purchase on offer off the pitch! Indian side would not be too disappointed with their bowling effort as they would have observed that it is looking like a good batting surface and there is very less help for the bowlers off the pitch. Jadeja provided the crucial breakthrough as Moeen Ali was dismissed just at the stroke of Tea. However, they will look to get England all out sooner rather than later and make sure that the hosts do not run away with the lead. Another interesting session awaits us. Can the England swell their lead with the tail in play now? Do join us at 1600 local (1500 GMT) for the final session to find out.

England would be the happier of the two sides going into Tea on Day 2. They have managed to go past India's total and they are in the ascendency now. Ollie Pope has stood tall when his side needed him the most and he was also able to stitch a couple of good partnerships with Bairstow and Moeen Ali. Although Bairstow was dismissed soon after play resumed post Lunch, Ali and Pope managed to steady the ship and took their side past India's total. But the former was sent back just before Tea. Which clearly took the advantage away from the hosts.

A well-fought session by both the sides. Bairstow could not last for long, but Ali made sure he filled his shoes and was on the charge from the word go. India looked lost in the middle but then a late breakthrough via Ravindra Jadeja got them back into the game. The second session is also shared amongst the two sides. England go back with a lead of 36 runs.

OUT! CAUGHT! Moeen Ali gives his wicket away. England change room wouldn't be happy about it. He was getting the runs but went for an unnecessary shot of looking to go big which proved to be a costly one. Ravindra Jadeja gets his first wicket of the game at such a crucial point. Floated full and outside off. Ali strides forward and looks to go big. But he does not middle it. The ball goes miles up in the air towards cover. Rohit Sharma settles under it and does the rest.
Commentary.Howout: c Rohit Sharma b Ravindra Jadeja

The second session is set to begin. Indian players stride out to the middle. Followed by Jonny Bairstow and Ollie Pope who come out to bat for England. Mohammed Siraj to start with the ball.

It is a see-saw game. This match is evenly poised yet again. The surface looks really good for batting at the moment. But can Jonny Bairstow ​​​​and Ollie Pope take advantage of it? To find out, do join us for the second session at 1340 local (1240 GMT).

A great comeback into the first team by Umesh Yadav! He has certainly made his presence felt in this Test match. He started the proceedings today by getting rid of Craig Overton, and it did not take much time as he struck in his first over itself. But in no time, Umesh Yadav got the better of Malan and put his side in the driving seat. But India lost grip over their advantage, as the bowlers struggled to trouble Pope and Bairstow and leaked way too many runs in the final hour of the session.

A surprise partnership to the rescue for England! The hosts did not start off well, as they lost their night watchman, Craig Overton, in the second over of the day. Soon after, Malan was sent back as he got his outside edge into play. But then, Pope and Bairstow, who were only dealing in boundaries at some point, stitched a crucial partnership of 77 runs to take their team to safer shores.

It was a really good session of cricket. In my opinion the first session was shared between the two sides. India started well this morning, but a crucial partnership between Pope and Bairstow made sure they put the pressure back on the visitors. England go back with a trail of 52 runs.

PITCH REPORT - Dominic Cork is down for a pitch report. He says that there is a bit of a cloud cover on. The pitch has slightly changed its colour. Adds that the wicket will get better for batting as the match progresses but the bowlers will also have some swing on offer.

India got off to a great start with the ball as they got rid of both the English openers inside four overs. Jasprit Bumrah was the pick of the bowlers as he picked two wickets in one over and put the hosts on the backfoot. But the biggest moment of the day came in the third session where Umesh castled England's in-form captain, Joe Root, with a beauty. England will start Day 2 on 53/3 with Dawid Malan and the night watchman Craig Overton at the crease. The first session would be very crucial for both sides as India would be looking to make early inroads and the hosts would look to lose as few wickets as possible and try and get settled in the middle.

Hello and a very warm welcome to Day 2 of the fourth Test match between India and England. It’s just been a single day in this 4th Test match, and we have seen 13 wickets fall, quite an eventful Day 1. The hosts bundled out India for 191 runs. They could’ve ended things early, but Shardul Thakur didn’t let them, as he knocked a brilliant half ton at the Oval to get his team to a respectable score. Do join us for the coverage of Day 2 as another riveting day of Test cricket awaits.
...Day 2, Session 1...

End of a fascinating day of Test cricket. 13 wickets fell on the first day of play and the match is wonderfully poised. England will be slightly happier as they dominated two out of the three sessions completely.

The trail is still 138 for the hosts, we have seen once Root goes, England's batting seems to fall apart and India will need that. The visitors will aim to get a couple of more wickets quickly on the morning of Day 2. For England, this is now a chance for the batters, who are yet to come, who are low in confidence to prove their mettle. One strong stand and England will be well and truly on top. Day 2 is generally the best day for batting. Can the hosts cash in or will we see the Indian bowlers roar yet again? Do join us at 11 am Local (10 am GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

It has been a day for the bowlers though, it was the English bowlers who did it earlier, Woakes and Robinson to be precise. Despite two fifties, one from Kohli to steady things and one from Thakur, which gave India's total some respectability, India finished with a score under 200. However, their bowlers have evoked belief back with three strikes in the last session of play. Exactly what India would have wanted by Stumps when they came out to bowl.

An excellent period of 17 overs from the Indian bowlers has got them right back in the game! It was Bumrah who started things off with two wickets in one over, getting rid of both the openers. However, Malan and Root then started scoring freely, the pitch seemed like it had no demons and the two batters turned the tide yet again in England's favor. But just as it seemed that both of them would walk out on Day 2 to bat, Umesh Yadav struck and got the big wicket of Root. That last wicket leaves the game beautifully poised.
Overton survives! Yorker, on off. But the tall pacer does well to dig it out. What a day of Test cricket this has been. It is Stumps on Day 1!

Full ball, on off. Malan blocks it solidly back to the bowler.
FOUR! EDGY! Full ball, outside off. Malan goes for the drive and gets the outside edge. The ball runs past the slip cordon and runs to the fence.
Length ball, on the pads. Malan flicks it away. Umesh Yadav runs across from fine leg to his right keeps it to two.
Very full again, on off. Malan blocks it back to the bowler.
Full ball, angling away from the off pole. Malan leaves this one.
Yorker, on off. Blocked out by Malan.
Shorter ball, down leg. Malan goes for the pull but does not middle. The ball goes past Pant and they get one.
Fuller ball, on off. Malan is solid in his defence of this one.
A touch fuller, outside off. Malan leaves it alone now.
Length ball, around off. Malan presses forward and blocks it well.
On a length, around off. Malan looks to block it but the ball goes past the outside edge.
Fuller ball, around off. Malan pushes it to covers.
Shorter ball, outside off. Left alone by Root.
Length ball, outside off. Root has no qualms in leaving this one.
FOUR! Lovely stroke! Length ball, outside off. Root plays it late and runs it between gully and third slip for a boundary. He will play that shot in his sleep and still score runs.
Short of a length, outside off. Root guides it with soft hands towards gully. The man gets across to his right and stops the ball.
Back of a length, around off. Root stays in the crease and blocks this one out.
Fuller ball, around off. Root comes forward and blocks it well.
Back of a length, around off. Malan hops up and blocks it.
Fuller ball, around off. Malan gets forward and defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Play and a miss! Shorter ball, outside off. Malan misses the cut.
Full ball, but wide outside off. Malan leaves this one alone.
A touch fuller and closer to the off pole. Malan blocks it from the crease.
Length ball, outside off. Left alone.
The English skipper, Joe Root, walks out to bat.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! The openers, who put up a 100-run stand in the previous game are back in the hut. Jasprit Bumrah is on fire. Two wickets in the over and India right back into this one. The extra bounce does the trick. This is shorter and outside off. Hameed looks to cut but due to the extra bounce, it goes off the outside edge and flies to Pant who takes it above his head.
Commentary.Howout: c Rishabh Pant b Jasprit Bumrah

Commentary.Commentary: Really well bowled! Shorter and just outside off, Hameed looks to defend initially but then the ball keeps rising, he lets it go.
Good length and on off, Hameed defends it onto the ground.
Malan is off the mark! Back of a length ball on off, this is pushed towards cover for one.
Dawid Malan walks out to bat.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! Jasprit Bumrah provides the perfect start for India! They desperately needed an early strike and have got it. Burns does not learn from his mistake on the previous ball. This is yet again on a length, closer to the off pole, lands and skids through. Burns once again looks to dab it late, it goes off the inside edge and this time onto the stumps.
Burns played that quite late! Length and on off, Burns looks to defend, he gets his bat down late. It goes off the bottom edge behind the wickets.
Another one which is well outside off, Hameed does not play at it.
Some away movement for Yadav but the line is outside off, left alone.
Yadav slips this one down the leg side, Hameed looks to flick but misses.
Three more! Fuller and outside off, Burns drives it through point. Three taken.
Back of a length and on off, Burns stands tall and blocks it.
Good length and just outside off, not played at.
One more nut outside off, Hameed does not play at it.
Yet another delivery outside off, Hameed lets it be.
Just outside off, Bumrah is getting it to zip through. Left alone.
That is a nasty delivery! This lands on a length, pitches, takes off and also holds its line. Hits the glove of Hameed as he tries to defend.
Outside off, some nice carry for Bumrah. Left alone.
Jasprit Bumrah to bowl now.
Angled in on middle, Hameed works it to sqaure leg.
A dot to end! A good start by Yadav! On the pads, this is worked to square leg.
Outside off, one more harmless ball. Not played at.
Another one on a length and just outside off, easy leave.
Another one on a length and just outside off. Burns shoulders arms to this one.
Yadav gets it right this time. Brings it back in from around off, defended nicely by Burns though.
England are underway and Burns is too! Angled into the pads, Burns works it through square leg. Two taken.
